one_line: Father-and-son court authors weaving the ornate Sanskrit romance Kadambari in 7th‑century Kannauj.

appearance.age_look: Bāṇa appears in his late 30s with a lean scholar’s build; Bhūṣaṇa looks mid‑20s, slightly slighter and more earnest.
appearance.face: Both share an oval face and warm medium‑brown complexion; Bāṇa has sharp, lively eyes, a defined nose, neatly trimmed mustache and short beard with a few stray lines, default expression a quick, amused focus; Bhūṣaṇa is softer‑featured and clean‑shaven, with large, reflective eyes and a calmer, attentive expression.
appearance.hair: Bāṇa’s black hair is drawn back into a tidy low knot at the back of the head, with a few short loose strands near the temples, and a simple narrow cream cloth band tied around the forehead; Bhūṣaṇa’s black hair is slightly longer and pulled into a higher, smaller knot without a band, with a single loose lock falling just in front of his right ear.
appearance.costume: Both wear modest, fully draped, era‑appropriate north Indian scholar attire inspired by 7th‑century courtly dress: Bāṇa in an ankle‑length off‑white cotton dhoti wrapped in tight, clean pleats, border edged with a thin maroon stripe, tied so it sits high on the waist and fully covers his legs; above, a light, long‑sleeved knee‑length kurta in pale cream with a subtle woven texture, side slits at the hip, and a narrow stand collar, over which is draped a soft, fine cotton shawl (uttariya) in muted saffron with a thin dark‑green edge, wrapped over his left shoulder and under his right arm in a scholarly style; he wears simple brown leather sandals, a single thin gold earring in his left ear, a narrow copper bangle on his right wrist, and a small wooden bead mala around his neck; Bhūṣaṇa echoes the silhouette but in lighter, slightly less ornate fashion: an ankle‑length light‑grey dhoti with a dark‑blue border, a pale blue long‑sleeved kurta with a slightly looser fit and no collar embroidery, and a soft white cotton shawl with a delicate sky‑blue edge draped over both shoulders and gathered in front, plus simple brown sandals and a single plain bronze bangle on his left wrist; both carry no armour, and their clothing is clean but shows faint creases from long hours seated, emphasizing scholarly practicality over display.
appearance.signature: A single large, slightly worn palm‑leaf manuscript bundle bound with dark cord and resting on a slim wooden writing board, with a reed pen and a small ink‑stained stylus corded to it, that Bāṇa usually holds tucked under his left arm while Bhūṣaṇa supports it from below with both hands.

ref_desc: Bāṇa and Bhūṣaṇabhaṭṭa are a lean, medium‑brown father and son with black hair in knots, Bāṇa mustached with a cream headband in off‑white dhoti, cream kurta and saffron shawl, Bhūṣaṇa clean‑shaven in grey dhoti, pale blue kurta and white‑blue shawl, jointly carrying a bound palm‑leaf manuscript bundle with reed pen in warm off‑white, saffron, pale blue, maroon and brown tones.
sheet_prompt: Draw a full‑body anime‑style model sheet of two related male Sanskrit authors from 7th‑century Kannauj, depicted together as a consistent pair: Bāṇa, late 30s, lean and medium‑brown, with an oval face, sharp lively eyes, neatly trimmed mustache and short beard, black hair pulled into a tidy low knot and a narrow cream cloth band around his forehead; and his son Bhūṣaṇabhaṭṭa, mid‑20s, slightly slighter, same complexion and oval face but softer, clean‑shaven, with large reflective eyes and black hair in a slightly higher small knot with one lock before his right ear. Show them in modest, fully draped, historically grounded scholar attire: Bāṇa in an ankle‑length off‑white cotton dhoti with a thin maroon border, tightly pleated and covering his legs, a pale cream long‑sleeved knee‑length kurta with a narrow stand collar, a muted saffron cotton shawl with a dark‑green edge draped over his left shoulder and under his right arm, simple brown sandals, a thin gold earring in his left ear, a copper bangle on his right wrist, and a small wooden bead mala at his neck; Bhūṣaṇa in an ankle‑length light‑grey dhoti with dark‑blue border, a pale blue long‑sleeved kurta with a loose fit and plain collar, and a soft white shawl with a sky‑blue edge draped over both shoulders and gathered in front, plus simple brown sandals and a plain bronze bangle on his left wrist. Their shared signature prop is a large, slightly worn palm‑leaf manuscript bundle bound with dark cord resting on a slim wooden writing board, with a reed pen and ink‑stained stylus tied to it; pose them so Bāṇa carries the bundle tucked under his left arm while Bhūṣaṇa supports it from below with both hands, emphasizing their collaborative storytelling. Use a warm palette of off‑white, saffron, pale blue, maroon and brown, and present them from multiple angles to clearly show face shapes, hair knots, draped garments and the manuscript bundle.
